artist.artist_description: Hank Snow was a Canadian country music artist born in 1914 in Nova Scotia. He began his career performing on local radio stations and rose to fame with hits like "I'm Moving On," which became a number one hit in 1950. Snow was inducted into the Country Music Hall of Fame in 1979, and interestingly, he was known for his yodeling style and his custom-built "Hank Snow White Gospel Ranger" guitar.

Simon & Garfunkel, an American folk rock duo from New York, formed in 1957 and rose to fame in the 1960s with hits like "The Sound of Silence" and "Bridge Over Troubled Water." Paul Simon and Art Garfunkel met in elementary school and began performing together as teenagers under the name Tom & Jerry. They won multiple Grammy Awards and were inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 1990, with their music continuing to influence generations.
